claim: In Multiple Sclerosis (MS) neurological disability results from myelin and axonal degeneration.
source: In Multiple Sclerosis (MS) neurological disability results from myelin and axonal degeneration.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work (Dutta and Trapp, 2011; Mahad et al., 2015).

claim: Inflammation-induced loss of myelin renders axons more susceptible to injury, leading to greater probability of permanent handicap and accumulated disease burden.
source: Inflammation-induced loss of myelin renders axons more susceptible to injury, leading to greater probability of permanent handicap and accumulated disease burden (Dutta and Trapp, 2011; Mahad et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Current therapeutic strategies aim at enhancing myelin repair.
source: Therefore, alongside available anti-inflammatory treatments, current therapeutic strategies aim at enhancing myelin repair.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work describing screening of repurposing molecules.

claim: Screening of repurposing molecules favoring proliferation, differentiation and maturation of endogenous oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) have been deployed.
source: In particular, screening of repurposing molecules favoring proliferation, differentiation and maturation of endogenous oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) have been deployed (Buckley et al., 2010; Deshmukh et al., 2013; Mei et al., 2014; Najm et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Two sources of OPCs exist in the adult mammalian brain: the resident parenchymal OPCs (pOPCs) and mouse subventricular zone-derived oligodendrocyte progenitors (SVZ-OPCs).
source: Endogenous myelin repair could exploit the two sources of OPCs that exist in the adult mammalian brain: the resident parenchymal OPCs (pOPCs) (Dawson et al., 2003; Tripathi et al., 2010; Wolswijk and Noble, 1989) and mouse subventricular zone-derived oligodendrocyte progenitors that then generate newly formed OPCs locally (SVZ-OPCs) (Nait-Oumesmar et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Remyelination from pOPCs produces thin myelin.
source: Remyelination from pOPCs is known to produce thin myelin (Xing et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: In pathological settings such as MS, limited remyelination produces so-called shadow plaques.
source: In pathological settings such as MS, this limited remyelination produces so-called shadow plaques (Franklin, 2002; Périer and Grégoire, 1965).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Autopsies of a large cohort of MS patients show complete remyelination in certain periventricular areas, as opposed to shadow plaques usually observed elsewhere in the brain and spinal cord.
source: However, autopsies of a large cohort of MS patients show complete remyelination in certain periventricular areas, that is, in the vicinity of the SVZ, as opposed to shadow plaques, usually observed elsewhere in the brain and spinal cord (Patrikios et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Examination of post-mortem MS brains revealed mobilization of human SVZ-OPCs.
source: Furthermore, examination of post-mortem MS brains revealed mobilization of human SVZ-OPCs (Nait-Oumesmar et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: In humans, endogenous remyelination driven by SVZ-OPCs can provide full remyelination.
source: Together, these observations suggest that in humans, endogenous remyelination driven by SVZ-OPCs can provide full remyelination.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from observations about periventricular remyelination and SVZ-OPC mobilization.

claim: In mice, SVZ-OPCs produce thicker myelin sheets, similar to those formed during normal development.
source: Supporting this concept, it has been recently shown in mice that SVZ-OPCs produce thicker myelin sheets, similar to those formed during normal development (Xing et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Stimulation of the regenerative potential of SVZ-OPCs could be a promising perspective for the development of therapies in the context of demyelinating diseases such as MS.
source: Therefore, stimulation of the regenerative potential of SVZ-OPCs could be a promising perspective for the development of therapies in the context of demyelinating diseases such as MS.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observations about SVZ-OPC remyelination capacity.

claim: In the adult rodent, Neural Stem Cells (NSC) localized in the SVZ neurogenic niche generate glial and neuronal progenitor cells.
source: In the adult rodent, Neural Stem Cells (NSC) localized in the SVZ neurogenic niche generate glial and neuronal progenitor cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Neuroblasts migrate tangentially toward the olfactory bulb through the rostral migratory stream (RMS) and differentiate as interneurons.
source: Neuroblasts migrate tangentially toward the olfactory bulb through the rostral migratory stream (RMS) and differentiate as interneurons (Doetsch et al., 1999; Lois and Alvarez-Buylla, 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Oligodendrocyte progenitor derived SVZ-OPCs migrate radially and tangentially into the corpus callosum (CC), striatum or cortex and differentiate into mature myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: In contrast, oligodendrocyte progenitor derived SVZ-OPCs migrate radially and tangentially into the corpus callosum (CC), striatum or cortex and differentiate into mature myelinating oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge about SVZ-OPC behavior.

claim: Under physiological conditions, production of SVZ-OPCs is lower compared with the number of neuroblasts that migrate along the RMS.
source: Under physiological conditions, production of SVZ-OPCs is lower compared with the number of neuroblasts that migrate along the RMS (Menn et al., 2006; Suzuki and Goldman, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: After a demyelinating insult or exposure to various extrinsic signals, NSC commitment switches towards production of oligodendrocyte progenitors that give rise to OPCs that migrate into the neighboring white matter.
source: However, after a demyelinating insult (Keirstead and Blakemore, 1999; Nait-Oumesmar et al., 1999) or exposure to various extrinsic signals (El Waly et al., 2014; Ortega et al., 2013), NSC commitment switches towards production of oligodendrocyte progenitors that give rise to OPCs that migrate into the neighboring white matter.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Stimuli favoring oligodendrocyte progenitor production include Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor signaling (EGFR).
source: Stimuli favoring oligodendrocyte progenitor production include Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor signaling (EGFR).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: EGFR overexpression in the adult rodent SVZ increases oligodendrogenesis under physiological and pathological conditions, facilitating brain recovery after demyelination.
source: EGFR overexpression in the adult rodent SVZ increases oligodendrogenesis under physiological and pathological conditions, facilitating brain recovery after demyelination (Aguirre et al., 2007; Doetsch et al., 2002; Scafidi et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: The continuous generation of neuronal and glial progenitors makes the adult SVZ a unique system in which to study the molecular mechanisms regulating stem cell fate decisions.
source: The continuous generation of neuronal and glial progenitors makes the adult SVZ a unique system in which to study the molecular mechanisms regulating stem cell fate decisions.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge about the SVZ.

claim: Thyroid hormone (TH) is a key homeostatic signal dynamically regulating neurogenesis.
source: Thyroid hormone (TH) is a key homeostatic signal dynamically regulating neurogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Within the neurogenic niches of the adult mammalian brain, TH regulates progenitor commitment to a neuronal fate.
source: Within the neurogenic niches of the adult mammalian brain, TH regulates progenitor commitment to a neuronal fate (Kapoor et al., 2015; López-Juárez et al., 2012), influencing learning, memory and mood (Kapoor et al., 2015; Remaud et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: T3, the active form of TH, and its nuclear receptor TRα1 promote NSC specification toward a neuronal identity in vivo through downregulation of the pluripotency gene Sox2 and the cell cycle genes Ccnd1 and Myc.
source: T3, the active form of TH, and its nuclear receptor TRα1 promote NSC specification toward a neuronal identity in vivo through downregulation of (i) the pluripotency gene Sox2 (López-Juárez et al., 2012; Remaud et al., 2014) and (ii) the cell cycle genes Ccnd1 and Myc (Lemkine et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: A thyroid hormone (T3)-free window, with or without a demyelinating insult, provides a favorable environment for SVZ-derived oligodendrocyte progenitor generation.
source: Here we report that a thyroid hormone (T3)-free window, with or without a demyelinating insult, provides a favorable environment for SVZ-derived oligodendrocyte progenitor generation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: After demyelination, oligodendrocytes derived from newly-formed progenitors provide functional remyelination, restoring normal conduction.
source: After demyelination, oligodendrocytes derived from these newly-formed progenitors provide functional remyelination, restoring normal conduction.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The cellular basis for neuronal versus glial determination in progenitors involves asymmetric partitioning of EGFR and TRα1, expression of which favor glio- and neuro-genesis, respectively.
source: The cellular basis for neuronal versus glial determination in progenitors involves asymmetric partitioning of EGFR and TRα1, expression of which favor glio- and neuro-genesis, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: EGFR+ oligodendrocyte progenitors, but not neuroblasts, express high levels of a T3-inactivating deiodinase, Dio3.
source: Moreover, EGFR+ oligodendrocyte progenitors, but not neuroblasts, express high levels of a T3-inactivating deiodinase, Dio3.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TRα absence with high levels of Dio3 provides double-pronged blockage of T3 action during glial lineage commitment.
source: Thus, TRα absence with high levels of Dio3 provides double-pronged blockage of T3 action during glial lineage commitment.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data about TRα1 and Dio3 expression patterns.

claim: Hypothyroidism was induced using MMI (0.1%) and NaClO4 (0.5%) during experimental demyelination induced by oral administration of cuprizone (CPZ).
source: Hypothyroidism was induced using MMI (0.1%) and NaClO4 (0.5%) during experimental demyelination induced by oral administration of cuprizone (CPZ) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: CPZ treatment causes marked demyelination in the corpus callosum.
source: CPZ treatment causes marked demyelination in the corpus callosum (Ludwin, 1978).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Four weeks of hypothyroidism were sufficient to stimulate significantly, and by nearly two-fold, oligodendrocyte progenitor numbers within the adult SVZ without affecting numbers of corpus callosum resident OPCs.
source: As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A four weeks of hypothyroidism were sufficient to stimulate significantly, and by nearly two-fold, oligodendrocyte progenitor numbers within the adult SVZ without affecting numbers of corpus callosum resident OPCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: CPZ-induced demyelination was accompanied by increased astrocytic (GFAP+) and microglial (IBA1+) responses.
source: CPZ-induced demyelination was accompanied by increased astrocytic (GFAP+) and microglial (IBA1+) responses (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Transitory hypothyroidism during demyelination, followed by T3/T4 pulses, increased Myelin Basic Protein (MBP) and Myelin Oligodendrocyte (MOG), two markers of maturing oligodendrocytes, in the corpus callosum and septum.
source: In accordance with our hypothesis, transitory hypothyroidism during demyelination, followed by T3/T4 pulses (Figure 1A) to favor oligodendrocyte maturation (Barres et al., 1994), increased Myelin Basic Protein (MBP) and Myelin Oligodendrocyte (MOG), two markers of maturing oligodendrocytes, in the corpus callosum and septum (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Transient hypothyroidism during demyelination increased OLIG2 expression in the corpus callosum.
source: Moreover, transient hypothyroidism during demyelination also increased OLIG2 expression in the corpus callosum (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: After 7 days of recovery, the number of OLIG2+ cells in the corpus callosum was decreased to 29.8 ± 10.6 OLIG2+ cells per 103 µm2 (p<0.05) in euthyroid CPZ-treated mice (EuCPZ), whereas values were not significantly different for controls (unexposed to CPZ) and hypothyroid CPZ-treated mice (HypoCPZ) (60 ± 8.1 and 44 ± 6.6 OLIG2+ cells per 103 µm2 respectively).
source: As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G, after 7 days of recovery, the number of OLIG2+ cells in the corpus callosum was decreased to 29.8 ± 10.6 OLIG2+ cells per 103 µm2 (p<0.05) in euthyroid CPZ-treated mice (EuCPZ), whereas values were not significantly different for controls (unexposed to CPZ) and hypothyroid CPZ-treated mice (HypoCPZ) (60 ± 8.1 and 44 ± 6.6 OLIG2+ cells per 103 µm2 respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: In HypoCPZ mice, a restricted lateral localization of the MBP+ and MOG+ cell masses was observed, above the dorsal part of lateral ventricles.
source: Interestingly, in the latter mice (HypoCPZ), we observed a restricted lateral localization of the MBP+ and MOG+ cell masses, above the dorsal part of lateral ventricles (see Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B for MBP and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F for MOG).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Applying the T3-free window during CPZ-induced demyelination increased cycling oligodendrocyte progenitor numbers in the SVZ, but decreased pOPC numbers in the corpus callosum.
source: Applying the T3-free window during CPZ-induced demyelination increased cycling oligodendrocyte progenitor numbers in the SVZ, but decreased pOPC numbers in the corpus callosum (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: TEM revealed increased myelinated axon density in the periventricular area of HypoCPZ versus EuCPZ.
source: TEM revealed increased myelinated axon density in the periventricular area of HypoCPZ versus EuCPZ (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The significant reduction in myelin thickness in EuCPZ (g = 0.83 ± 0.07) versus controls not subjected to demyelination (g = 0.75 ± 0.07, p<0.001) was rescued in HypoCPZ mice (g = 0.77 ± 0.06).
source: Further, evaluation of g-ratios representing myelin thickness with respect to axon diameter revealed that the significant reduction in myelin thickness in EuCPZ (g = 0.83 ± 0.07) versus controls not subjected to demyelination (g = 0.75 ± 0.07, p<0.001) was rescued in HypoCPZ mice (g = 0.77 ± 0.06) (Figure 1D,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The density of myelinated axons as well as the g-ratio and the myelin thickness were rescued in HypoCPZ compared to EuCPZ treated-mice when mice in each group only received a saline solution (NaCl) after cuprizone treatment.
source: As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–E, the density of myelinated axons as well as the g-ratio and the myelin thickness were also rescued in HypoCPZ compared to EuCPZ treated-mice when mice in each group only received a saline solution (NaCl) after cuprizone treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The fast component of CAPs was significantly reduced in EuCPZ mice compared to controls, but completely rescued in HypoCPZ mice.
source: Comparison of normalized CAP amplitudes revealed that the fast component was significantly reduced in EuCPZ mice compared to controls, but completely rescued in HypoCPZ mice (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The normalized area under the curve of the fast component (f-AUC) was smaller in EuCPZ mice, but regained control values in HypoCPZ mice.
source: Furthermore, the normalized area under the curve of the fast component (f-AUC) was smaller in EuCPZ mice, but regained control values in HypoCPZ mice (Figure 2D,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: This functional improvement was correlated with higher MBP expression levels in recorded slices of HypoCPZ mice.
source: This functional improvement was correlated with higher MBP expression levels in recorded slices of HypoCPZ mice (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: These experiments indicate an extensive functional recovery of demyelinated fibers after transient hypothyroidism.
source: These experiments indicate an extensive functional recovery of demyelinated fibers after transient hypothyroidism.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the CAP recording data.

claim: TRα (βgal+) was strongly expressed in cells positive for DCX but excluded from OLIG2+ cells.
source: Using the Thra-lacZ mouse (Macchia et al., 2001), we showed that TRα (βgal+) was strongly expressed in cells positive for DCX (Figure 3A,D) a neuronal lineage marker (Sapir et al., 2000) but excluded from OLIG2+ cells (Figure 3A,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: In wild-type mice, TRα1 was excluded from SOX10+ cells, that are also OLIG2+.
source: In wild-type mice, TRα1 was also excluded from SOX10+ cells, that are also OLIG2+ (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: In vitro studies showed that TRα1 co-localized with TUJ1 but could be found in more mature OPCs expressing O4.
source: Further, in vitro studies showed that TRα1 co-localized with other neuronal markers such as TUJ1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) but could be found in more mature OPCs expressing O4, another oligodendroglial marker (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,C').
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: EGFR co-localized with OLIG2, but was excluded from DCX+ cells.
source: As expected, EGFR, a major gliogenic factor (Aguirre et al., 2007), co-localized with OLIG2, but was excluded from DCX+ cells (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: TRα1 is expressed in neural lineage cells whereas EGFR is more restricted to glial lineage cells in the adult SVZ.
source: These experiments show that TRα1 is expressed in neural lineage cells whereas EGFR is more restricted to glial lineage cells in the adult SVZ.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data about TRα1 and EGFR expression patterns.

claim: T3 repressed Egfr.
source: T3 treatment repressed Egfr (Figure 3E) whereas hypothyroidism significantly increased SVZ Egfr mRNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Hypothyroidism significantly increased SVZ Egfr mRNA.
source: T3 treatment repressed Egfr (Figure 3E) whereas hypothyroidism significantly increased SVZ Egfr mRNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: EGFR+ SVZ cell numbers were significantly increased in mice lacking TRα1 (TRα°/° mice).
source: In parallel, EGFR+ SVZ cell numbers were significantly increased in mice lacking TRα1 (TRα°/° mice) (Gauthier et al., 2001) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Using an in vitro neurosphere assay, T3 decreased by about two-fold the numbers of EGFR + cells after 7d differentiation.
source: Lastly, using an in vitro neurosphere assay, we observed that T3 decreased by about two-fold the numbers of EGFR + cells after 7d differentiation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: T3 repressed transcription from the wild-type Egfr promoter, whereas mutating a negative Thyroid Hormone Response Element (TRE) in the Egfr promoter abolished T3/TRα1 repression.
source: T3 repressed transcription from the wild-type Egfr promoter, whereas mutating a negative Thyroid Hormone Response Element (TRE) in the Egfr promoter abolished T3/TRα1 repression (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Loss of function using shTRα1 increased Egfr promoter activity whereas gain of function with a TRα1-encoding plasmid repressed transcription.
source: Loss of function using shTRα1 increased Egfr promoter activity (Figure 3G, left) whereas gain of function with a TRα1-encoding plasmid repressed transcription (Figure 3G, right).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Egfr is a negative T3-regulated gene in the adult SVZ.
source: Thus, Egfr is a negative T3-regulated gene in the adult SVZ.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data about T3 effects on Egfr expression.

claim: TRα1 was found in 80% (±2%) of dividing cells, but was unequally distributed in 11% (±3.6%) of these.
source: TRα1 was found in 80% (±2%) of dividing cells, but was unequally distributed in 11% (±3.6%) of these (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: In cells with unequal TRα1 distribution, TRα1 localized to a polarized crescent in prophase, segregating preferentially to one daughter cell in telophase.
source: In these, TRα1 localized to a polarized crescent in prophase (Figure 4A,A'), segregating preferentially to one daughter cell in telophase (Figure 4B,B').
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: EGFR localized asymmetrically in mitotic cells, forming a crescent opposite that of TRα1 during prophase.
source: As previously reported (Sun et al., 2005), EGFR localized asymmetrically in mitotic cells (see Figure 4C for a representative telophase), forming a crescent opposite that of TRα1 during prophase (Figure 4D,D').
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures and a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: One daughter cell preferentially inherits TRα1 and the other, EGFR.
source: Hence, one daughter cell preferentially inherits TRα1 and the other, EGFR (see telophase, Figure 4E,E').
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Within the specific SOX2+ mitotic progenitor population, asymmetric TRα1 localization was observed in 20% (±3.4%) of these SOX2 + cells.
source: Lastly, within the specific SOX2+ mitotic progenitor population, asymmetric TRα1 localization was observed in 20% (±3.4%) of these SOX2 + cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: This smaller proportion of cells displaying asymmetric TRα1 matches the oligodendrocyte versus neuron ratio produced in the adult SVZ in normal conditions, with the large majority of cells being neuronal.
source: This smaller proportion of cells displaying asymmetric TRα1 matches the oligodendrocyte versus neuron ratio produced in the adult SVZ in normal conditions, with the large majority of cells being neuronal (Menn et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Dio3 was strongly expressed in SVZ-NSCs co-expressing Nestin and SOX2.
source: Dio3 was strongly expressed in SVZ-NSCs co-expressing Nestin and SOX2 (Figure 5A) or GFAP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Dio3 expression was strongest in EGFR+ and SOX2+ progenitors and absent from DCX+ neuroblasts.
source: Furthermore, Dio3 expression was strongest in EGFR+ (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) and SOX2+ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D) progenitors and absent from DCX+ neuroblasts (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: In the Pdgfrα:GFP mouse, PDGFRα+ OPCs were still Dio3 positive.
source: In the Pdgfrα:GFP mouse (Hamilton et al., 2003), PDGFRα+ OPCs were still Dio3 positive (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Strong co-expression of EGFR/Dio3 was confirmed in vitro, using adult SVZ neurosphere cultures: in basal conditions, DCX+ cells had barely detectable Dio3 as opposed to strongly Dio3 expressing-EGFR+ cells.
source: Strong co-expression of EGFR/Dio3 was confirmed in vitro, using adult SVZ neurosphere cultures: in basal conditions, DCX+ cells had barely detectable Dio3 as opposed to strongly Dio3 expressing-EGFR+ cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Down-regulating Dio3 expression by shDio3 significantly reduced cell proliferation by 50% and numbers of OLIG2+oligodendrocyte progenitors by 30%.
source: Down-regulating Dio3 expression by shDio3 significantly reduced cell proliferation by 50% (shctl: 9.2 ± 0.6 versus shDio3: 4.6 ± 0.8, p=0.0097, Figure 5D) and numbers of OLIG2+oligodendrocyte progenitors by 30% (shctl: 55.5 ± 5.8 versus shDio3: 35 ± 6.6, p=0.032, Figure 5E), showing that down-regulation of Dio3 is sufficient to modulate oligodendrogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: A 24 h, T3 (1 nM to 50 nM) pulse added before cell differentiation, promoted DCX+ neuronal genesis at the expense of OLIG2+ populations.
source: A 24 h, T3 (1 nM to 50 nM) pulse added before cell differentiation, promoted DCX+ neuronal genesis at the expense of OLIG2+ populations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: T3 (1 nM) decreased five-fold the ratio of OLIG2+versus DCX+ cell numbers.
source: T3 (1 nM) decreased five-fold the ratio of OLIG2+versus DCX+ cell numbers (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Type three deiodinase, preferentially expressed in oligodendrocyte progenitors, maintains oligodendrogenesis in the adult SVZ.
source: Bringing together these in vivo and in vitro results shows that type three deiodinase, preferentially expressed in oligodendrocyte progenitors, maintains oligodendrogenesis in the adult SVZ.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data about Dio3 expression and function.

claim: Transient hypothyroidism stimulates oligodendrocyte production, by favoring oligodendrocyte progenitor lineage decisions.
source: These results show that transient hypothyroidism stimulates oligodendrocyte production, by favoring oligodendrocyte progenitor lineage decisions (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A T3-free window promoted SVZ-derived oligodendrocyte progenitor and OPC generation followed by functional remyelination in response to a demyelinating insult.
source: We demonstrated that a T3-free window promoted SVZ-derived oligodendrocyte progenitor and OPC generation followed by functional remyelination in response to a demyelinating insult.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: SVZ-OPC-driven remyelination, as opposed to resident adult pOPC-derived remyelination, resulted in wrapping of denuded axons with myelin of normal thickness, restoring functional nerve conduction.
source: In accordance with others studies SVZ-OPC-driven remyelination, as opposed to resident adult pOPC-derived remyelination, resulted in wrapping of denuded axons with myelin of normal thickness, restoring functional nerve conduction.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and citations to other scholarly work.

claim: SVZ-derived OPCs are more prone to participate to efficient brain remyelination than resident OPCs.
source: Our results strongly suggest that SVZ-derived OPCs are more prone to participate to efficient brain remyelination than resident OPCs.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: During adult neurogenesis, the neuron versus glia cell fate decision in newly derived NSC progenitors is determined respectively by the presence or absence of both TRα1 and, T3, its ligand.
source: We show that during adult neurogenesis, the neuron versus glia cell fate decision in newly derived NSC progenitors is determined respectively by the presence or absence of both TRα1 and, T3, its ligand.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Absence of TRα1 in oligodendrocyte progenitors is ensured by asymmetric segregation during mitosis of TRα1, a neurogenic factor and EGFR, an established inductor of oligodendrogenesis.
source: Absence of TRα1 in oligodendrocyte progenitors is ensured by asymmetric segregation during mitosis of TRα1, a neurogenic factor (López-Juárez et al., 2012) and EGFR, an established inductor of oligodendrogenesis (Aguirre et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Absence of the ligand, T3, in the EGFR + oligodendrocyte progenitors is ensured by high levels of Dio3, the T3 inactivating deiodinase.
source: Absence of the ligand, T3, in the EGFR + oligodendrocyte progenitors is ensured by high levels of Dio3, the T3 inactivating deiodinase (St Germain et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: This oligodendrocyte progenitor-specific Dio3 expression restricts TH availability in the glial lineage.
source: This oligodendrocyte progenitor-specific Dio3 expression restricts TH availability in the glial lineage.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data about Dio3 expression patterns.

claim: Transient hypothyroidism favors lineage determination of adult multipotential SVZ-progenitors towards an oligodendroglial fate and promotes functional brain remyelination in vivo.
source: Taken together, the data provide evidence that transient hypothyroidism favors lineage determination of adult multipotential SVZ-progenitors towards an oligodendroglial fate and promotes functional brain remyelination in vivo.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Addition of T3 following a period of hypothyroidism consolidates remyelination.
source: As expected, addition of T3 following a period of hypothyroidism consolidates remyelination (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Transient hypothyroidism during demyelination, prior to the addition of T3, activates oligodendrogenesis in the dorsal SVZ favoring migration of remyelinating OPCs into the corpus callosum.
source: Strikingly, our data indicate that transient hypothyroidism during demyelination, prior to the addition of T3, activates oligodendrogenesis in the dorsal SVZ favoring migration of remyelinating OPCs into the corpus callosum.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cell tracing using a eGFP lentivirus showed that the remyelinating OPCs derive from the SVZ.
source: First, cell tracing using a eGFP lentivirus showed that the remyelinating OPCs derive from the SVZ.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from lentiviral tracing experiments.

claim: A hypothyroid window (without cuprizone treatment) was sufficient to bolster significantly SVZ-OPCs and not resident pOPCs.
source: Second, a hypothyroid window (without cuprizone treatment) was sufficient to bolster significantly SVZ-OPCs and not resident pOPCs.
